plans.title: Fielding Focus — Station Night
plans.summary: Station-based fielding practice with warm-up competition, 3 simultaneous drill stations, team situational defense, and a hitting block to close.
plans.notes: 3 coaches running simultaneous stations. Players rotate every 10 minutes through 2 infield stations and 1 outfield station.

blocks.details: Full team on the outfield grass. Jog, high knees, butt kicks, shuffles, arm circles, torso twists, wrist/finger stretches.
coachingPoints: Keep it controlled — this isn't a race
Big arm circles forward and backward, 10 each direction
Finish with wrist circles and finger stretches

blocks.details: Partner catch starting at 30 ft, backing up to 60 ft then 90 ft. Competition: track passed balls and errant throws per pair. Pair with fewest errors wins. Keeps reps sharp and competitive.

drillLinks.label: A Throwing Routine For All Youth Baseball Players

coachingPoints: Four-seam grip on every throw
Step toward your target — don't just arm it
Follow through: throwing hand finishes near the opposite hip
Scorekeeping: each dropped ball or throw that bounces before your partner counts as 1 point (low score wins)

blocks.activity: Station Rotation — 3 Simultaneous Stations (10 min each, rotate twice)
blocks.details:
Split players into 3 groups. Each coach runs one station. Groups rotate every 10 minutes so everyone hits all 3 stations.

📍 STATION 1 — Infield: Ground Ball Fundamentals (Coach 1)
Focus on athletic ready position, approaching the ball, and funneling with two hands. Mix in straight-on, forehand, and slow roller reps.

📍 STATION 2 — Infield: Backhand Ground Ball Drill (Coach 2)
Focus exclusively on balls to the throwing-hand side. Crossover step, glove angle (fingers down), field off the right foot, quick throw.

📍 STATION 3 — Outfield: Drop Step Fly Ball Drill (Coach 3)
Coach calls L/R or signals deep. Player drop steps, tracks ball over the shoulder, catches while moving forward. Finish with a crow hop throw back.

drillLinks.label: Station 1: How to Field a Ground Ball in 3 Easy Steps
Station 1: 3 Simple Baseball Fielding Drills for Youth Players
Station 2: How To Field a Ground Ball Backhand
Station 3: 3 Great Outfield Drills for Youth Players
Station 3: Outfield Drills You MUST Be Doing!

coachingPoints: Station 1: Field out front, funnel to the belly button, two hands when possible
Station 2: Crossover first — don't reach. Fingers DOWN on the backhand.
Station 3: Drop step immediately — no backpedaling. Call the ball every rep.
Rotate on coach's whistle. Reset and be ready before the next rep comes.

blocks.details: Full defense on the field. Coach announces the situation and hits fungoes. Place 1-2 base runners. Defense must communicate, make the correct play, and back each other up — just like a real game. Mix in cutoffs, relay reads, and force plays.

drillLinks.label: Game-Like Drills for Efficient Baseball Practice

coachingPoints: Everyone has a job on every play — no spectators
Talk before the pitch: 'Where am I going with this ball?'
Back-up responsibilities matter as much as the primary play
Reset after each play — don't carry a mistake into the next one

blocks.details: Coach pitches from flat ground or short mound. Rotate batters every 5-6 pitches. Fielders in the field making live plays on balls in play. Suggested round structure: Round 1 — hit it where it's pitched; Round 2 — opposite field focus; Round 3 — situational (runner on 3rd, less than 2 outs — get the run in).
coachingPoints: Keep the fielders engaged — they're taking reps too
Situational round: if they pull an opposite-field pitch, that's a win too — process over result
Keep the line moving, minimize standing around

blocks.activity: Position Group: 2B & SS — Double Play Work
blocks.details: 2B and SS stay after while others are dismissed. Focus exclusively on double play feeds and pivots. Coach hits ground balls to third or first; middle infielders work the feed to second and relay to first. Alternate who covers the bag.

drillLinks.label: How to Turn a Double Play — 3 Steps for Youth Players
Double Play Drills with Bill Ripken
Double Play Infield Tips and Drills (Antonelli Baseball)

coachingPoints: Get to the bag EARLY — you need to be set before the throw arrives
Inside pivot (ball from 3B side): catch, drag the bag, throw
Outside pivot (ball from 1B side): catch, step around, throw
Short, quick throw to first — no wind-up. Get rid of it.

plans.coachNotes: 3 coaches needed for station rotation (0:15-0:45). Assign your most experienced coach to Station 2 (backhand) — it needs the most technical feedback. After practice, only need 1 coach to stay for the 2B/SS optional block.
